intent: To illustrate the increasing trend of very unfavorable attitudes between Democrats and Republicans towards each other from 1994 to 2016.

requirements.question: Is the overall 1994-to-2016 increase for both series required, or is only one party's trend required?
Must the clip convey step-by-step monotonic increase, or is a single start-to-end upward trend sufficient?
Is it required to identify 2016 as the peak for both series, or only to show an increase?

units.claim: Both series have a higher relative_value in 2016 than in 1994, showing an overall upward trend.
accept: The 2016 relative_value is higher than the 1994 relative_value for both series.
Each series shows an upward trajectory over the full period.
units.evidence: Both series must show an increase from the first time point to the last.

units.claim: Within each series, relative_value increases at every successive measured year: 1994 < 2008 < 2014 < 2016.

basis.note: first measured year in Series A
second measured year in Series A
third measured year in Series A
fourth measured year in Series A
first measured year in Series B
second measured year in Series B
third measured year in Series B
fourth measured year in Series B

accept: Values rise at each measured step for both series.
No measured year is lower than the previous measured year in either series.
units.evidence: Each series must show monotonic upward progression across the four displayed time points.

units.claim: For both series, the maximum relative_value in the displayed period occurs at 2016: 0.5129 for Series A and 0.5408 for Series B.

basis.note: maximum in Series A; earlier values are 0.1492, 0.3450, 0.4010
maximum in Series B; earlier values are 0.1585, 0.2985, 0.4290

accept: The 2016 value is the highest for each series.
The displayed period ends at the series highs: 0.5129 and 0.5408.
units.evidence: The final year 2016 must be visibly the highest point in both series.

optional_valid: Ordering flip: Series A is higher than Series B at 2008 (0.3450 vs 0.2985), while Series B is higher at 1994 (0.1585 vs 0.1492), 2014 (0.4290 vs 0.4010), and 2016 (0.5408 vs 0.5129).

Largest annualized relative_value increase for both series occurs in the shortest final interval 2014–2016 (Series A: (0.5129 - 0.4010) / 2 = 0.05595 per year; Series B: (0.5408 - 0.4290) / 2 = 0.0559 per year).

g0_data_completeness.selection: all role=bar data rows; annotation rows excluded

hardcases.handling: Requires human visual inspection before semantic scoring.
